catalog_quote: The vowels are also typical of this group. There are 7 oral and 5 nasalized vowels, as illustrated by the words in Table 2. ... all vowels have nasalized allophones when adjacent to nasal consonants. There are three contrasting tones, symbolized as shown in Table 3, with the mid tone being left unmarked. ... Table 3. Contrasting tones in Tee. High bé fight, war / Mid be home / Low bè enclose, make a fence around

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding sentence and Table 3 are verbatim in the held UCLA WPP 91 scan at the stated pages (p.85 text, p.86 Table 3; scanned pg-088/ plus for the diacritics). (2) The deciding source is a first-hand 1995 phonetic study by Ladefoged, authoritative for what it says (three contrastive level tones, minimal triplet) but only 4 pages and not about prosody, so 'no stress rule described' is an argument from a very short text. (3) Glottolog registers no grammar or sketch for Tee (Glottolog's fullest description is a phonology or text collection); the one open descriptive item beyond Ladefoged, Anyanwu & Omego 2015, was downloaded now and independently restates the H/M/L system with the same triplet (p.3), adds moraic syllable structure and prefix-triggered tone spreading, and never mentions stress or accent -- it confirms the 'tonal' coding and shows tone is lexically and morphologically contrastive.

sources.quote: "There are three phonemic tones which are high, mid and low as shown by the following words which display tonal contrast. 5a) be 'fight (noun)' b) be 'home' c) be 'fence'" ... "In Tee, a syllable may be either mono-moraic or polymoraic." The rest of the paper describes M- and L-tone spreading from nominalizing prefixes onto H-tone verb roots. The words 'stress' and 'accent' occur nowhere in the paper (a full-text search for stress/accent found nothing).
sources.locator: p.3, section 1, examples (5a-c) and following paragraph on syllable structure; tone-spreading rules pp.4-9
sources.note: Independent native-region linguists' description restating the three-tone system (p.3) with tone-spreading rules and syllable/mora structure; corroborates the Ladefoged-based 'tonal' coding and shows tone is lexical and morphologically active. downloaded now.
